thread.title: Congressman Moylan urges withdrawal of VA policy affecting disability claim evaluations
thread.title_full: Congressman Moylan urges withdrawal of VA policy affecting disability claim evaluations

author: h. s. wilkins
title: Congressman Moylan urges withdrawal of VA policy affecting disability claim evaluations
text:
Congressman James Moylan has called on Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins to withdraw a new Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) policy that changes how disability claims are evaluated for veterans receiving medication or treatment.
The interim final rule, which took effect on February 17, 2026, alters the process for determining disability ratings for new claims and requests for increased ratings. Under the new regulation, the VA will assess a veteran’s level of impairment based on their condition while taking prescribed medication or undergoing treatment. If these interventions lessen symptoms, this improvement may be reflected in a lower disability rating. The change does not impact veterans who already have an established disability rating but does apply to existing pending claims, including those from Guam.
In a letter addressed to Secretary Collins, Congressman Moylan requested that the VA withdraw the rule to prevent any disadvantage to veterans.
“I strongly oppose any policy that risks lowering or undervaluing the compensation our veterans earned through their service,” said Congressman Moylan. “Veterans who responsibly manage their health should not face unintended consequences in the benefits process.”
Moylan also urged veterans not to delay seeking medical care or filing claims due to concerns about how their conditions might be evaluated under the new rule.
“I encourage veterans to continue seeking treatment and to file claims as appropriate,” he stated. “No veteran should hesitate to get care out of concern about how their condition will be evaluated. My office remains committed to advocating for fair treatment and standing with our veteran community.”
Veterans needing assistance can contact Congressman Moylan’s District Office at (671) 922-6673.
